## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical, real-world sysadmin tasks: LVM planning, filesystem layout, boot/root considerations, firewall and SELinux configuration, and user privilege management.

## Key Concepts
- LVM: pvcreate, vgcreate, lvcreate
- Filesystems: XFS and fstab
- Security: SELinux enforcing and wheel-based sudo
- Networking: firewalld http/https rules

## Code Example
```bash
pvcreate /dev/sda
vgcreate rhel /dev/sda
lvcreate -L40G -n root rhel
lvcreate -L40G -n home rhel
lvcreate -L40G -n var rhel
mkfs.xfs /dev/rhel/root
mkfs.xfs /dev/rhel/home
mkfs.xfs /dev/rhel/var
mount /dev/rhel/root /
mkdir -p /home /var
mount /dev/rhel/home /home
mount /dev/rhel/var /var
# /etc/fstab entries would reference /dev/rhel/... set here
systemctl enable --now firewalld
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=http
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=https
firewall-cmd --reload
setenforce 1
sed -i 's/^SELINUX=.*/SELINUX=enforcing/' /etc/selinux/config
useradd -m dev
usermod -aG wheel dev
```

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement repeatable, isolated health checks using systemd timers, a common admin task, with correct permissions and log hygiene.

## Key Concepts
- systemd: service vs timer; OnCalendar scheduling
- non-login users and minimal privileges
- file-based host list and basic ping
- log rotation using logrotate
- idempotent setup and basic testing

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
HOSTS=$(grep -v '^#' /etc/hosthealth.conf || true)
for h in $HOSTS; do
  if ping -c1 -W1 "$h" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    status="OK"
  else
    status="DOWN"
  fi
  echo "$(date --iso-8601=seconds) $h $status" >> /var/log/hosthealth/summary.log
done
```

```systemd
# /etc/systemd/system/hosthealth.service
[Unit]
Description=Host health check

[Service]
User=hosthealth
ExecStart=/home/hosthealth/health.sh
```

```systemd
# /etc/systemd/system/hosthealth.timer
[Unit]
Description=Daily host health check

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

```bash
# /etc/logrotate.d/hosthealth
(/var/log/hosthealth/summary.log) {
  weekly
  rotate 4
  compress
  missingok
  notifempty
  copytruncate
}
```

Follow-up questions
- How would you handle a large host list to avoid long ping times?
- How would you alert on consecutive DOWN results and integrate with existing monitoring?

## Key Concepts

- Service continuity (reload vs restart)
- TLS validation (openssl s_client)
- Config preservation (certs, /etc/httpd)

## Code Example

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose a scheduled health check using a non-root user, a systemd timer, and log rotation, mirroring real maintenance tasks.

## Key Concepts
- systemd timer and service pairing
- non-login system users
- logrotate configuration and log hygiene

## Code Example
```bash
# health.sh (as /opt/health/health.sh)
#!/bin/bash
TS=$(date '+%F %T')
OUT="/var/log/health/health.log"
(</dev/tcp/localhost/22) >/dev/null 2>&1; P22=$?
(</dev/tcp/localhost/80) >/dev/null 2>&1; P80=$?
echo "$TS port22=$([ $P22 -eq 0 ] && echo OPEN || echo CLOSED) port80=$([ $P80 -eq 0 ] && echo OPEN || echo CLOSED)" >> "$OUT"
```
```ini
# healthcheck.service
[Unit]
Description=Health check
[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=health
ExecStart=/opt/health/health.sh
```
```ini
# healthcheck.timer
[Unit]
Description=Health check every 5 minutes
[Timer]
OnUnitActiveSec=5min
Unit=healthcheck.service
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```
```text
# /etc/logrotate.d/health
 /var/log/health/health.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  missingok
  notifempty
  compress
  delaycompress
  create 0640 health health
 }
```
